slot.brief: A lens of known glass placed in a liquid of given refractive index; find the new focal length or determine whether it acts as a converging or diverging lens.

stem: A convex glass lens has focal length $+20\ \text{cm}$ in air and refractive index $1.4$. It is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.5$. What are its focal length and nature?

verdicts.working: For a thin lens, power scales with (n_lens/n_medium − 1). Thus 1/f_liquid = (1/20) × [((1.4/1.5) − 1)/(1.4 − 1)] = −1/120 cm⁻¹, so f = −120 cm and the lens diverges.

working:
$$\frac{f_\ell}{f_a}=\frac{n_g-1}{\frac{n_g}{n_\ell}-1}=\frac{0.4}{\frac{14}{15}-1}=-6,\qquad f_\ell=-6(20\ \text{cm})=-120\ \text{cm}.$$ Negative focal length means the lens is diverging.

Independent check: For a thin lens, power scales with (n_lens/n_medium − 1). Thus 1/f_liquid = (1/20) × [((1.4/1.5) − 1)/(1.4 − 1)] = −1/120 cm⁻¹, so f = −120 cm and the lens diverges.
